exam.title: 2023年12月大学英语六级真题(第1套) 仔细阅读与篇章精研

passages.title: Passage One: Behavioral Nudges and Consumer Autonomy
passages.content:
In modern behavioral economics, the concept of the "nudge"—a subtle modification in the choice architecture designed to predictably steer people's decisions without forbidding any options or altering economic incentives—has achieved widespread acclaim. Pioneered by Nobel laureate Richard Thaler and legal scholar Cass Sunstein, nudges have been enthusiastically adopted by public health authorities, tax administrations, and environmental agencies to promote retirement savings, organ donation, and energy conservation. By capitalizing on human cognitive shortcuts, such as status quo bias and default options, governments have achieved remarkable policy goals at minimal fiscal expense.

However, the rapid migration of nudging into commercial digital ecosystems has sparked fierce ethical contention. Tech conglomerates and e-commerce platforms have weaponized behavioral insights into what critics dub "dark patterns"—manipulative interface designs that exploit cognitive vulnerabilities to extract consumer data, manipulate purchasing decisions, and prolong screen addiction. From pre-ticked subscription renewal boxes to artificial countdown timers creating synthetic urgency, commercial nudges rarely serve consumer welfare; instead, they covertly prioritize shareholder profits at the expense of consumer autonomy.

Ethical philosophers argue that even benevolent nudges subtly undermine individual moral agency. When choice architects exploit human irrationality rather than presenting rational arguments, they treat citizens as passive psychological subjects rather than autonomous moral agents capable of reasoned deliberation.

As digital nudging grows increasingly sophisticated through real-time machine learning, the boundary between benign guidance and psychological coercion has blurred. Safeguarding democratic autonomy in the algorithmic age requires robust consumer protection laws that prohibit deceptive digital architectures and restore genuine self-determination to market participants.

passages.title: Passage Two: The Fragility of Global Supply Chains
passages.content:
For nearly four decades, the governing philosophy of multinational manufacturing was anchored to the tenets of hyper-globalization and hyper-efficiency. Corporate executives, incentivized by quarterly earnings benchmarks, systematically re-engineered supply networks according to "just-in-time" inventory models. Production was offshored to developing regions with rock-bottom labor expenses, inventory buffers were slashed to near-zero, and logistics were calibrated with microscopic precision across oceans and continents. For consumers, this model delivered an unprecedented cornucopia of affordable consumer goods, ranging from semiconductors to athletic footwear.

However, the unprecedented convergence of geopolitical friction, pandemic disruptions, extreme climate shocks, and transport chokepoints has brutally laid bare the profound vulnerability of hyper-optimized supply chains. What was hailed as lean efficiency during tranquil periods revealed itself as brittle fragility in the face of systemic turbulence. When a single semiconductor hub shuttered or an essential maritime canal was blocked, production lines ground to a halt thousands of miles away, precipitating worldwide inflationary spirals and shortages of critical medical supplies.

In boardrooms and policy circles, the pendulum is now decisively swinging from "just-in-time" efficiency to "just-in-case" resilience. Corporations are diversifying supplier bases, nearshoring production facilities closer to end markets, and building strategic buffer inventories of mission-critical components. Concurrently, national governments are treating supply chain sovereignty as an urgent national security imperative, subsidizing domestic semiconductor fabrication and rare earth processing.

Yet, this retreat from hyper-globalization carries substantial economic tradeoffs. Building redundant capacity and reshoring manufacturing inevitably raises baseline production costs, threatening to lock in structurally higher consumer inflation. Navigating this new geopolitical economic epoch will require striking a delicate balance between defensive resilience and global cooperative efficiency.

questions.stem: What was the initial objective of 'nudges' in public policy?

options.text: To steer citizens toward beneficial decisions without restricting their choices.
To impose punitive financial penalties on unhealthy behaviors.
To eliminate the need for legislative debate in parliament.
To privatize public healthcare and retirement systems.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】事实细节题。第一段说明'nudge'的初衷是'steer people's decisions without forbidding any options or altering economic incentives'，在不剥夺选择权的前提下引导有益决策，故选A。

questions.stem: What was the core principle guiding multinational manufacturing over past decades?

options.text: Maximizing domestic employment in developed nations.
Prioritizing hyper-efficiency and 'just-in-time' inventory models.
Maintaining huge stockpiles of emergency industrial components.
Restricting trade strictly to neighboring geographic regions.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】事实细节题。第一段首句即指出'anchored to the tenets of hyper-globalization and hyper-efficiency... just-in-time inventory models'，追求超高效率与零库存准时制，故选B。

questions.stem: How do commercial 'dark patterns' differ from benevolent public policy nudges?

options.text: They are completely illegal in every sovereign country.
They exploit cognitive weaknesses to maximize corporate profits.
They require users to pass complex cognitive tests before purchasing.
They are designed exclusively for elderly demographic groups.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】对比分析题。第二段指出商业'暗黑模式'是'manipulative interface designs that exploit cognitive vulnerabilities... prioritize shareholder profits'，压榨消费者漏洞为商业牟利，故选B。

questions.stem: What has exposed the inherent fragility of global supply chains?

options.text: A sudden worldwide surge in consumer demand for luxury goods.
Geopolitical tensions, pandemic shocks, and environmental disruptions.
The invention of decentralized 3D printing technology.
The total depletion of global petroleum and oil reserves.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】因果事实题。第二段指出'geopolitical friction, pandemic disruptions, extreme climate shocks, and transport chokepoints'无情揭露了超精益供应链的脆弱性，故选B。

questions.stem: What philosophical objection is raised against even well-intentioned nudging in paragraph 3?

options.text: It costs taxpayers exorbitant sums of money to implement.
It treats individuals as passive subjects rather than reasoned moral agents.
It is ineffective in modifying long-term human habits.
It encourages citizens to distrust elected officials.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】哲学论点题。第三段指出即使是善意的助推'treat citizens as passive psychological subjects rather than autonomous moral agents capable of reasoned deliberation'，贬损了自主理性，故选B。

questions.stem: What strategic shift is currently occurring in corporate supply-chain planning?

options.text: A transition from 'just-in-time' efficiency to 'just-in-case' resilience.
An aggressive push to offshore all remaining manufacturing to polar regions.
The complete abandonment of supplier contracts in favor of spot markets.
A total freeze on foreign capital investment across all industries.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】战略转变题。第三段明确写道'the pendulum is now decisively swinging from just-in-time efficiency to just-in-case resilience'，从极致效率转向防御性韧性，故选A。

questions.stem: How are national governments responding to supply-chain vulnerabilities?

options.text: By subsidizing domestic fabrication of critical semiconductors and materials.
By penalizing domestic companies that purchase locally produced goods.
By deregulating corporate shipping monopolies completely.
By eliminating all strategic reserves of petroleum and grain.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】政府举措题。第三段指出'national governments are treating supply chain sovereignty as an urgent national security imperative, subsidizing domestic semiconductor fabrication'，故选A。

questions.stem: What has aggravated the threat of commercial nudges in recent years?

options.text: The integration of real-time machine learning into interface designs.
The total collapse of consumer protection courts.
The decline of digital advertising expenditure.
A global drop in smartphone ownership rates.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】事实理解题。第四段首句提到'As digital nudging grows increasingly sophisticated through real-time machine learning'，机器学习的结合使其更具隐蔽威力和胁迫性，故选A。

questions.stem: What remedy does the author advocate in the final paragraph?

options.text: Dismantling behavioral economics departments in universities.
Enacting robust consumer protection regulations to ban deceptive architectures.
Relying strictly on corporate voluntary codes of conduct.
Mandating that consumers pass psychology courses before buying online.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】对策结论题。末段指出保护民主自主性需要'robust consumer protection laws that prohibit deceptive digital architectures'，通过强有力的法规禁止欺骗性界面设计，故选B。

questions.stem: What economic consequence might arise from reshoring and building redundant capacity?

options.text: A rapid deflationary collapse in consumer prices.
Structurally higher production costs and consumer inflation.
Immediate elimination of all international maritime shipping.
An instantaneous doubling of corporate profit margins.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】经济代价题。最后一段指出重构成本是'inevitably raises baseline production costs, threatening to lock in structurally higher consumer inflation'，造成长期结构性通胀上升，故选B。
